The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 767a5eb7cd819af7), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 19. statement: If Theorem 1.1 fails, there is a sequence of dimensions and centered compactly supported log-concave laws µ satisfying Equation (3.1). Fix s = 1/8, form µs, bs, Ms, Ks as in Equation (3.3), and put λ = R−1 s . After passage to a subsequence there are smooth positive probabilities η and smooth vector fields w such that, with A = Aη and I = Eη|w|2, λ −→ 1, R(η) ≤ λ−1 , 0 < I < ∞, w ∈ Dom(A)n , (3.28) Aw = (λId − Ks)w, ∥(A − 1)w∥L2(η) + |Eηw| = o( √ I), (3.29) Eη|Ksw|2 = o(I), Eη|Dw|2 = (1 + o(1))I. (3.30) The spectral gap of A is at least λ. Each coordinate function belongs to Dom(A). Exactly one of the following constructions can be used throughout the subsequence: (i) Rs > RP s , η = f2µs for the positive unit-norm optimizer, w = D log f2, and I = 2λH(η | µs). The exact deficit identity in Equation (3.15) holds for compact square-root tests relative to η, and AY = (Y − bs)/s − w. (ii) Rs = RP s , η = µs, Aφ = λφ, Eηφ = 0, w = Dφ, and I = λEηφ2. One may rescale φ so that I → 0. All o-terms refer to the counterexample sequence with fixed finite parameters. In particular no relation between dimension, I, and the rate of convergence is asserted or needed here.
